newsitem.title: INDIA: India eases investment rules for state insurers.
newsitem.headline: India eases investment rules for state insurers.

text.p: The Indian cabinet on Tuesday granted greater autonomy to Life Insurance Corp of India (LIC) and General Insurance Corp of India (GIC), both state-owned, to make investments.

The government said in a statement that the cabinet approved a proposal to exempt LIC from seeking prior government approval for making "individual, non-scheduled, non-consortium investments beyond 100 million rupees subject to prudential norms".
It said the cabinet exempted GIC from seeking prior government approval for making "individual 'unapproved' investments beyond 50 million rupees subject to prudential norms".
The statement said the decisions would grant "increased autonomy to both LIC and GIC to improve their functional efficiency".
